# Native Geometry on Apple Silicon {#native-geometry-on-apple-silicon}

ARIA-NBV uses the public PyTorch3D API on every platform. A maintained
[PyTorch3D fork](https://github.com/JanDuchscherer104/pytorch3d) adds native
Mojo forward kernels beside the existing CPU and CUDA implementations. ARIA-NBV
does not carry a second renderer or point--mesh implementation.

Set one environment variable before starting a process:

```sh
export PYTORCH3D_BACKEND=mojo
```

| Value | Geometry placement and dispatch |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | Uses Mojo for eligible CPU forward calls when the extension is present; otherwise uses the matching PyTorch3D CPU or CUDA implementation. |
| `cuda` | Selects CUDA geometry and requires CUDA tensors plus a CUDA-enabled PyTorch3D build. |
| `mojo` | Selects CPU-resident geometry and requires every accelerated call to satisfy the Mojo contract. Unsupported calls fail instead of silently changing backend. |
| `cpu` | Selects the compiled PyTorch3D CPU reference implementation. |

`mojo` is the recommended data-generation setting on Apple Silicon because it
makes incomplete coverage visible. `auto` is useful for mixed workloads that
intentionally allow reference fallbacks.

## Architecture {#architecture}

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["ARIA-NBV public PyTorch3D calls"] --> S["PYTORCH3D_BACKEND"]
  S -->|"cuda"| C["existing PyTorch3D CUDA kernels"]
  S -->|"mojo"| M["native Mojo forward kernels"]
  S -->|"cpu"| R["existing PyTorch3D CPU kernels"]
  S -->|"auto"| E["eligible-call dispatch"]
  E --> M
  E --> C
  E --> R
```

The dispatch seam lives in `pytorch3d/_mojo_ops.py`. ARIA-NBV only uses the
switch to choose the corresponding geometry device; rendering, pose generation,
RRI scoring, VIN-store generation, and multi-step rollout generation continue to
call normal PyTorch3D functions.

The accelerated implementation is genuine Mojo source compiled into the
Python-importable `pytorch3d._mojo` module:

- `pytorch3d/csrc/mojo/_mojo.mojo` defines the Python extension module.
- `pytorch3d/csrc/point_mesh/point_mesh_mojo.mojo` implements point-to-face and face-to-point distance.
- `pytorch3d/csrc/rasterize_meshes/rasterize_meshes_mojo.mojo` implements mesh rasterization.

No ARIA-NBV-specific C++ or header bridge is required.

## Supported Mojo Contracts {#supported-mojo-contracts}

The Mojo path currently covers the forward operations used by ARIA-NBV data
generation:

| Operation | Supported contract |
| --- | --- |
| Point-to-face distance | Contiguous CPU `float32` points shaped `[P, 3]`, contiguous CPU `float32` triangles shaped `[T, 3, 3]`, matching contiguous CPU `int64` batch-start arrays, and no input gradients. |
| Face-to-point distance | The same packed, ragged-batch tensor contract as point-to-face distance. |
| Mesh rasterization | Contiguous CPU `float32` face vertices shaped `[F, 3, 3]`; contiguous one-dimensional CPU `int64` mesh metadata; positive image dimensions; `blur_radius=0`, `faces_per_pixel=1`, `bin_size=0`, perspective correction enabled, barycentric clipping disabled, backface culling disabled, and no face-vertex gradients. |

Public PyTorch3D clipping and original-face remapping remain outside the kernel
and can feed the supported rasterizer contract. Backward/autograd kernels,
soft or multi-face rasterization, binned rasterization, other dtypes, and GPU
tensors are not Mojo contracts. `auto` delegates those cases to upstream
PyTorch3D; `mojo` rejects them.

## Apple Silicon Setup {#apple-silicon-setup}

Use macOS 15 or newer, Xcode 16 or newer, and an arm64 Python 3.11 interpreter;
these are the current [official Mojo system requirements](https://docs.modular.com/mojo/requirements/).
Keep the `uv` environment outside a cloud-synchronized checkout. The lockfile
pins the Apple Silicon Mojo compiler and runtime used to build the fork, and the
fork targets the portable `apple-m1` CPU baseline for M1--M5 compatibility.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/JanDuchscherer104/ARIA-NBV.git
cd ARIA-NBV
git submodule update --init --recursive

cd aria_nbv
export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="$HOME/.cache/aria-nbv/venv"
uv sync --locked
```

Confirm the native module and strict dispatch before generating data:

```sh
PYTORCH3D_BACKEND=mojo uv run --locked python - <<'PY'
from pytorch3d import _mojo_ops

assert _mojo_ops.has_mojo(), "PyTorch3D was built without the Mojo module"
print("pytorch3d_mojo_ok")
PY
```

If the assertion fails after changing the pinned fork revision, force a clean
PyTorch3D rebuild with `uv sync --locked --reinstall-package pytorch3d`.

## VIN Store and Multi-Step Rollouts {#vin-store-and-multi-step-rollouts}

The backend switch belongs on the process invocation; individual ARIA-NBV
configs do not need backend-specific copies.

```sh
cd aria_nbv

# One-sample VIN-store profile; remove --dry-run after checking paths and assets.
PYTORCH3D_BACKEND=mojo uv run --locked nbv-build-offline \
  --config-path ../.configs/build_vin_offline_81286_backend_smoke.toml --dry-run
PYTORCH3D_BACKEND=mojo uv run --locked nbv-build-offline \
  --config-path ../.configs/build_vin_offline_81286_backend_smoke.toml

# Multi-step rollout profile.
PYTORCH3D_BACKEND=mojo uv run --locked nbv-build-rollouts \
  --config-path ../.configs/build_rollouts_v1_smoke.toml --dry-run
PYTORCH3D_BACKEND=mojo uv run --locked nbv-build-rollouts \
  --config-path ../.configs/build_rollouts_v1_smoke.toml
```

These commands still require the ASE source data, mesh assets, offline source
store, and model checkpoints named by their configs. The switch changes the
PyTorch3D geometry backend, not the data contract or output schema.

For CUDA runs, use the same commands with `PYTORCH3D_BACKEND=cuda` in the Linux
CUDA environment. Use `cpu` only as a reference or diagnostic backend.

## Equivalence and Runtime Evidence {#equivalence-and-runtime-evidence}

Kernel equivalence is checked against the compiled PyTorch3D CPU reference with
fixed edge cases and randomized holdouts. The checks cover ragged and empty
batches, ties, degenerate geometry, clipping/remapping, face-index equality, and
numeric tolerances for distances, depth, barycentric coordinates, and pixel
distances. End-to-end checks additionally exercise pose generation, depth
rendering, VIN-store writing, and repeated multi-step rollout generation.

Runtime comparisons must be read as hardware-specific measurements. The report
records the host, backend, workload shape, warm-up, repetitions, and output
equivalence status; it does not treat measurements from different machines as a
direct hardware speedup claim.

## Current Limitations {#current-limitations}

- Native Mojo support is pinned to arm64 macOS and the Mojo version in the ARIA-NBV lockfile.
- The accelerated contracts are forward-only and deliberately narrow around ARIA-NBV data generation.
- VIN training, optional xFormers, and the PointNeXt extension remain separate from these PyTorch3D geometry kernels.
- CUDA and Apple Silicon measurements require their respective hosts; missing measurements are reported as missing, never inferred.
